Localized trade-wind convergence and shallow, transient trade-wind
troughs continue to bring periods of low-end scattered showers to the
islands. Tinian and Saipan will see patchy scattered showers this 
evening, before a plume of drier air moves in from the east. CIMSS 
Mimic Precipitable Water imagery shows precipitable water totals of 
1.5 to 2 inches across the Marianas, decreasing to 1.1 inches 
upstream. Although well south-southwest of the area, Tropical Storm 
Hagupit will provide enough moisture and trailing convergence to 
support increased potential for scattered showers at Guam and Rota 
this weekend, though a signal remains weak. Starting Monday, the 
remnants of Invest 94W will gradually lift west-northwest across Yap 
State, with the broad disturbance looking to skirt just southwest of 
the Marianas. This will bring additional chances at scattered showers
and isolated thunderstorms through the first half of next week.

Marine/Surf...
High pressure north of the region and a strengthening Tropical
Storm Hagupit to the south-southwest will bring mostly fresh 
trade winds through tonight, before easing slightly to moderate to 
fresh Friday. This will maintain combined seas around 7 to 10 
feet through at least Friday afternoon, so the Small Craft 
Advisory was extended. Additionally, light south-southeast swell 
from TS Hagupit will continue over the next day or so, diminishing 
Saturday as the storm moves farther southwest of the Marianas. Trade 
winds and swell will gradually ease this weekend, and combined seas 
will diminish by several feet through the early half of next week.

There is a high risk of rip currents along east and north facing 
reefs due to the elevated east trade swell, which is wrapping around
the islands to bring hazardous surf of 9 feet along north-facing 
reefs. As the trade swell begins to ease slightly, the reduced wrap-
around will allow surf to diminish below hazardous levels late 
Friday afternoon. However, trade swell, and associated surf along 
east-facing reefs, will remain sufficiently elevated to maintain a 
high risk of rip currents along east facing reefs through the next 
few days.

Tropical Systems...
At 400 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Hagupit (05W) was
located near 7.5N 142.9E, roughly 70 miles west of Woleai, 135 miles
southwest of Faraulep, and 225 miles southeast of Fais in Yap State.
Himawari visible satellite late this afternoon continues to show a
disorganized, lopsided storm with a broad area of moderate to deep
convection focused along its north to southeast flanks. Bands of 
heavy showers and thunderstorms are seen throughout the convergent 
inflow into TS Hagupit, further to the east and southeast, covering 
much of eastern Yap State. Although Hagupit remains weak and
asymmetrical, it has shown slightly better organization today with
more robust convective development about the center.

TS Hagupit is moving west-northwest at 11 mph, and is expected to
maintain this speed as it continues west-northwestward through the
next day or so. Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph. Hagupit
is forecast to maintain this intensity through tonight before
gradually strengthening Friday through Saturday, remaining a low-end 
tropical storm through the next few days. Hagupit is expected to 
reach peak intensity on Saturday as it passes somewhere between Yap
and Ngulu in western Yap State, and is less favored to become a 
strong tropical storm at this time. As of late this afternoon, a 
Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Faraulep, Woleai, Ulithi
and Fais in Yap State. Additionally, a Tropical Storm Watch remains 
in effect for Yap and adjacent coastal waters, and Ngulu in Yap 
State.

For more information on Tropical Storm Hagupit, please refer to 
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header 
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header 
WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
An embedded NET disturbance (formerly Invest 94W) and the
Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) continue to be the primary
weather makers across eastern Micronesia. A significant southerly
surge along the eastern peripheries of said disturbance is expected
to pummel Kosrae with near gale-force gusts and intense showers
overnight, followed by slowly improving conditions the next few days, 
as the system moves downstream and allows more diffuse trades to move
in by the weekend. Pohnpei will continue to see more convective 
cycles the next few days, as the sharpest convergence zone builds 
overhead and becomes enhanced by stronger trades bringing periods of 
intense showers and some thunderstorms. Another surge in the ITCZ is
building right over Majuro, bringing near gale-force gusts along with
occasionally heavy showers overnight, followed by decreasing shower
coverage until a moderately drier trade-wind regime returns by early
next week.
